subject: FinCorp: intermittent 503s on long streaming sessions — triage + temporary escape-hatch

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>

Subject: FinCorp: intermittent 503s on long streaming sessions — triage + temporary escape-hatch

Hi team,

Spoke to Donna this morning — FinCorp is seeing intermittent 503s that surface during long streaming chat sessions (sessions > 20 minutes, sustained token rates). They reported this across two environments (staging and prod) and have a live demo next Wednesday.

What they have provided: small log bundle (attached), a CSV of trace IDs with timestamps, and a screenshot of the 503. The customer is in mid-deal and this is blocking their last integration demo.

Ask: can runtime/platform confirm whether there's a known failure mode for long-lived streaming connections and whether we can expose a temporary toggle or routing escape-hatch (session-affinity or a higher in-flight cap) that Sales can flip per-account while engineering investigates a proper fix? If not, what's the fastest mitigation path (route to dedicated pool, short polling fallback, etc.)?

Required: we need a realistic mitigation plan + owner by EOD so I can update Donna and schedule a short sync.

Attachments: fincorp_fwd_logs_20261119.txt, fincorp_trace_ids_20261119.csv, screenshot_503_20261119.png

Thanks — K

--
Kimberly Park
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.com

From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: Donna Patton <donna.patton@fincorp.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 11:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: FinCorp: intermittent 503s on long streaming sessions — triage + temporary escape-hatch

Thanks Kimberly — I pulled the attachments and skimmed the trace IDs. Quick notes up front:

- Preliminary signal: the 503s align with proxy-level connection resets that correlate with large KV cache growth for a subset of sessions (long context + frequent sampling). Not definitive yet; need the full span traces from their ingress.
- Immediate, low-risk mitigations we can consider exposing as a per-account toggle: 
  1) session_affinity=true — keep sessions on a single serving worker to avoid cross-worker KV misses (helps for long KV-heavy sessions).
  2) backpressure_max_inflight=150 (current default 64 in hosted) — raises the in-flight token cap for that account for short window.
  3) route_to_dedicated_pool — move them to a dedicated node pool with pinned KV cache if they have available committed capacity.

I can prototype a canary toggle endpoint that flips (1) + (2) within a day, but we should validate against load in staging. The platform change to expose a per-account flag requires a small config surface+RBAC check — I'd estimate 2–3 days to ship safely (with canary). If we only need a temporary manual flip we can do it faster via an operator-side config change (45–90 minutes) but that requires runbook and an opt-in window.

Next steps I need from Sales/Customer: full request headers and proxy spans for a few of the trace IDs attached, and confirmation whether they will accept being routed to a dedicated pool for the demo.

I will start a quick spike to reproduce in staging.

— Logan

--
Logan Wright
Runtime Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: FinCorp: intermittent 503s on long streaming sessions — triage + temporary escape-hatch

Appreciate the details, Logan. A couple of product/roadmap asks and constraints to call out before we do an operator flip:

1) We should treat this as a candidate for a short-term "escape hatch" feature we can expose under the customer settings page: session affinity + in-flight cap. That aligns with other customers' asks. However, public toggles need audit logs and an RBAC guard.

2) For the demo next Wednesday, operator-side routing to a dedicated pool is acceptable. If we do that, make sure we add a short TTL on routing (auto-revert) and an opt-in flag so we don't create stale pinned sessions.

3) Acceptance criteria for the customer: no 5xxs during the 45-minute demo window and end-to-end latency under their current SLA during that time. Please confirm what telemetry we will watch and who will be on the bridge.

I can prioritize a small product ticket to spec the escape-hatch (scope: UI flag + backend switch + audit log) — target for initial doc by next Tue, delivery estimate 2 sprints if engineering confirms low-risk. If Logan can do the operator flip today we should treat that as mitigation only.

Marissa
Product Manager, Redwood Inference

Donna — can you confirm a staging window tomorrow (Mon) between 10:00–14:00 PST? If we validate there, Logan says operator flip can be applied for a short window and we'll add auto-revert.

I'll create a short calendar invite and add the runbook once Logan shares it. Appreciate the quick turn on this.
